rationale: Each of the 6766 works has one passage, so a work's rate is 0 or 1 for DISTANCE_TRAVEL. Late means year >= 1876. I took the late-minus-early mean within each of the 8 genres, then averaged the genres with equal weight: effect +0.0021. The 95% CI, [-0.021, 0.025], comes from a bootstrap of works resampled within each genre-period cell (2000 reps). Genres disagree on direction: adventure, juvenile, romance and domestic_realist go down a little, while sensation_mystery and other go up. The estimate's sign flips under robustness checks: high-confidence dates only give +0.003, high plus medium give -0.005, dropping 'other' gives -0.005, a 1866 cutoff gives -0.010 and an 1886 cutoff gives +0.004. Decade means fall from the early 1800s to the 1870s and then rise again, which is not one monotonic change at the cutoff. The early period is thin; small early genre cells, some with about 40-50 works, widen the uncertainty. Other things that could create or hide a difference: genre mix within periods, uneven dating precision, and noise in the passage annotations. The cited passages are early and late examples tagged DISTANCE_TRAVEL; they show the construct but do not establish a trend. Conclusion: no robust shift at this cutoff.
